title: Gas appliances: recognising gas components and stopping work safely
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Victorian BPC, Servicing Type A gas appliances (AS 4575) (no date shown); NSW Government, Gasfitter compliance and regulatory obligations (last updated 9 April 2026); Queensland Building and Construction Commission, Gasfitting (last published 2 November 2026; last reviewed 31 August 2021); WA Building and Energy, Having gasfitting work done (last updated 23 November 2024); ACT Government, Gas appliance workers (no date shown; only part of this page has been confirmed); Consumer and Business Services (SA), Plumbing, gas fitting or electrical contractors licence (no date shown); Victorian Building Authority, AS/NZS 5601.1 gas installations (no date shown; mandatory date confirmed).
audience: Workers who clean the outside of appliances that may be gas-fired, such as commercial ovens, fryers, combi units and some dishwashers and laundry machines
learningOutcomes: Identify the gas components on an appliance that are outside the scope of this course
Recognise the signs of a gas leak, incomplete combustion and ignition risk
Describe the stop, evacuate and report sequence for a suspected gas leak
Explain which gas work needs a licensed or registered gasfitter or plumber, and why this course does not grant it

instruction.heading: Which parts of a gas appliance are off limits
instruction.body: Many commercial ovens, fryers, combi ovens, some dishwashers and laundry machines use gas for heating. Gas components include the burner and burner tray, the pilot or igniter, the flame sensor, the gas valve, the regulator, the gas supply pipe and its flexible connector, the flue and the flue outlet. Under this course you do not clean, touch, adjust or remove any of these. You may clean the outside surfaces of a gas appliance, but you keep clear of the gas supply connector and the flue, and you do not wipe or spray near the burner openings or the igniter. Where the manufacturer's care instructions say that a gas component must be cleaned by a qualified person, the instruction governs and the task is excluded. Cleaning or servicing gas appliances is regulated work. In Victoria, internal cleaning of a Type A unit under AS 4575 counts as covered work, and only plumbers holding the specialised Type A servicing class may do it (no page date shown). A cleaner who opens the appliance is doing work they are not authorised to do.

instruction.heading: Recognising a gas leak and an unsafe flame
instruction.body: A gas leak may show as a distinct smell, often described as rotten eggs, a hissing sound near a connector or valve, a dead or dying plant near a pipe, or a bubbling in a wet area near a line. Incomplete combustion can show as a yellow or sooty flame, scorch marks around a burner, a soot deposit on a surface, or a headache or dizziness among people in the room. Any of these is a reason to stop. Do not light, relight or operate the appliance, do not operate electrical switches or tools in the area, and do not use a flame or spark to check for a leak. Increase ventilation only if you can do so without any risk of ignition. Keep people clear of the area and report the situation immediately to the site contact.

instruction.heading: The stop, evacuate and report sequence
instruction.body: If you suspect a gas leak, stop all work at once. Do not switch any device on or off, including lights and extraction fans. Move people out of the area and keep them clear of the appliance and the pipe. Make the area safe to leave by closing an accessible manual gas valve only if the site procedure tells you to do so and you can reach it without any risk. Call the emergency number for the gas supplier or the emergency services from outside the area, and tell the site contact. Do not re-enter until the emergency responder has said that the area is safe. Afterwards, record what you saw and smelled, the time, the people involved, and the actions taken. Do not attempt to fix a leak, tighten a fitting or replace a flexible connector, because those are gasfitting tasks.

procedure: Before you clean, identify whether the appliance is gas-fired from its data plate, its burner area, or the site contact's information.
Mark the gas components as excluded on the job record, including the burner, igniter, valve, regulator, connector and flue.
Keep water, cloths and spray away from the burner openings, igniter and gas connector. Do not clean inside the burner area.
Look and smell before you start for any sign of a gas leak or incomplete combustion, and do not use a flame or spark to check.
If you notice a sign of a leak or unsafe flame, stop, do not operate any switch, move people clear, and report to the site contact and the emergency number from outside the area.
Refer any gas component fault, damage or cleaning request to the owner's gas servicing provider, and record the referral.
Record the gas-appliance check and the referral, and do not return to any gas component until the appropriate person has inspected it.

workedExamples.situation: You are cleaning the outside of a commercial fryer. You notice a faint rotten-egg smell near the gas connector at the back and the connector looks dusty.
workedExamples.reasoning: A smell that suggests gas is a stop sign. Stop work, do not operate the fryer's controls or any switch or tool, and do not use a flame or spark. Move people away from the area and tell the site contact. Call the gas emergency line or emergency services from outside the area. Do not touch the connector or try to tighten it. Record what you noticed and the time, and wait for the responder before any work resumes.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial oven's burner area is sooty and the booking asks you to clean the oven's burner tray so the oven looks good.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the burner tray in scope?
workedExamples.reasoning: The burner tray is a gas component. Cleaning it is gas appliance servicing and is outside this course. Decline that part, complete the external clean away from the burner openings, and record the soot deposit with a photograph. Refer the burner tray to the owner's gas servicing provider. Do not use a brush or chemical in the burner area.

equipmentAndPpe: Site emergency contact information, including the gas supplier's emergency number, recorded in the job
Gas leak awareness card or the site's gas emergency procedure
No flame, spark or ignition source is to be used to check for gas

commonErrors.error: Cleaning the burner tray or igniter because the appliance looks dirty.
commonErrors.prevention: Burner, igniter, valve and flue are gas components and are excluded. Refer them.

commonErrors.error: Checking a suspected gas leak with a lighter, a match or a flame.
commonErrors.prevention: Never use a flame or spark. Stop, evacuate, and report from outside the area.

commonErrors.error: Operating an electrical switch or extraction fan after smelling gas.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not operate any switch or electrical device in the area. Leave and call for help from outside.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A gas leak or an incomplete combustion event can cause fire, explosion and carbon monoxide exposure. Treat any sign as an emergency and stop work.

Gas appliance servicing and internal cleaning are regulated work. Victoria: the specialised plumbing class covers internal cleaning of Type A units. NSW says gasfitting needs a licence. Queensland's gasfitting occupational licence, issued by the Chief Gas Examiner, covers servicing a gas system. Western Australia says all gasfitting work must be done by a licensed gasfitter. The ACT requires anyone doing gas appliance work to hold a licence. South Australia's combined licence covers gas fitting downstream of the meter.

Gas installation work follows AS/NZS 5601.1. Victoria's VBA says the 2022 edition became mandatory for gasfitters from 30 March 2023 (no page date shown). This lesson does not grant a gasfitting licence or any authority to work on gas components.

qualityStandard: Gas components are recorded as excluded before any cleaning starts
No cleaning cloth, spray or brush enters the burner area, igniter or gas connector
Any sign of a leak or unsafe flame stops the job immediately and is reported
documentationEvidence: The record that the appliance is gas-fired and the gas components marked excluded
A photograph of any soot, scorch or connector condition observed
The referral made to the gas servicing provider, and the emergency actions taken if a leak was suspected
summary: Gas burners, igniters, valves, regulators, connectors and flues are outside the cleaning scope.
A gas smell, hiss or unsafe flame means stop, do not operate switches, evacuate, and call for help from outside.
Gas servicing and internal cleaning need the right registration or licence, which this course does not grant.

knowledgeChecks.question: You notice a rotten-egg smell near the gas connector of a commercial fryer. What is the first action?
options: Turn on the extraction fan to clear the smell, then carry on working if the room looks clear
Stop work, do not operate any switch, move people clear, and call for help from outside the area
Tighten the connector to stop the leak, then carry on with the clean once the smell has gone
Light a match to check where the gas is coming from, since a small flame is the safest test

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part is a gas component that a cleaner must not clean?
options: The stainless steel front panel
The outside of the glass door
The burner tray and igniter
The drip tray under the door

knowledgeChecks.question: What does a yellow or sooty flame on a gas appliance indicate?
options: A correctly adjusted flame that needs no action from the cleaner
A cleaning product residue that is harmless and burns off
A normal sign that the appliance is ready for cleaning
Possible incomplete combustion, which is a reason to stop and refer

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does completing this course not allow a cleaner to clean a gas burner?
options: Because the course does not grant a gasfitting or gas-servicing authority, and burner cleaning is regulated gas work
Because the course does not cover appliance surfaces at all, so no cleaning of any gas unit is taught
Because burners are always cleaned by the owner, who holds the gas licence for the site and its equipment
Because burners do not need cleaning under any rule, so there is no task to carry out for the gas unit

knowledgeChecks.question: In Victoria, which group is authorised to carry out internal cleaning of a Type A gas appliance under AS 4575?
options: Any cleaner who has completed a short appliance cleaning course and their induction
Registered plumbers holding the specialised class for Type A appliance servicing
Any person who holds a general building licence, including those for renovation work
The customer, after reading the manufacturer's manual for the appliance and the gas fittings

officialReferences.title: Servicing Type A gas appliances (AS 4575)
officialReferences.covers: Victoria only. Internal cleaning of a Type A appliance is covered work for plumbers in the specialised class. Publisher: Building and Plumbing Commission (Victoria).

officialReferences.title: Gasfitter compliance and regulatory obligations
officialReferences.covers: A licence is needed for any gasfitting work. Certificates of compliance go to Building Commission NSW. Servicing and cleaning of appliances are not addressed. Publisher: NSW Government (Building Commission NSW).

officialReferences.title: Gasfitting
officialReferences.pageDate: Last published 2 November 2026; last reviewed 31 August 2021
officialReferences.covers: The gasfitting occupational licence is issued by the Chief Gas Examiner and Resources Safety and Health Queensland, not by QBCC. Scope includes servicing a gas system. Publisher: Queensland Building and Construction Commission (page); licence issued by the Chief Gas Examiner.

officialReferences.title: Having gasfitting work done
officialReferences.covers: All gasfitting work must be carried out by a licensed gasfitter. Building and Energy issues the licence. Servicing and cleaning are not addressed. Publisher: Government of Western Australia (Building and Energy).

officialReferences.title: Gas appliance workers
officialReferences.covers: Anyone doing gas appliance work in the ACT must hold a licence. No licence class is named on the page. Publisher: ACT Government (ACT Planning; names Access Canberra).

officialReferences.title: Plumbing, gas fitting or electrical contractors licence
officialReferences.covers: Consumer and Business Services administers this licence. It covers electrical work on appliances and gas fitting downstream of the meter. Publisher: Business.gov.au (ABLIS) listing for the South Australian Government.

officialReferences.title: AS/NZS 5601.1 gas installations
officialReferences.covers: Victoria only. The 2022 edition became mandatory for relevant gasfitting work from 30 March 2023. Publisher: Victorian Building Authority.
